newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 7.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet will discuss the possibility of raising natural gas prices. Transgas, which has a monopoly for importing natural gas, is experiencing financial difficulties since it must pay for gas in dollars but has been selling the resource on the domestic market at fixed crown prices.

- Companies affected by flooding will probably not receive direct assistance from the government, but instead will receive loans guaranteed by the government. The government also plans to issue a second tranche of flood bonds.

- The Finance Ministry announced that investors have purchased half of the first tranche of flood bonds which went on sale at all major commercial banks last week. Ceska Sporitelna leads by selling 215 million crowns worth, followed by Komercni Banka and IPB.

- IPB announced that as of Friday it will be lowering minimum interest rates on existing and newly issued medium and longterm loans by one percentage point. Interest rates on shorterm loans will be lowered by half a percentage point.

- Benzina a.s. the largest domestic gasoline distributor will not raise its prices at its pumps this week despite Ceska Rafinerska raising its wholesale prices. Ceska Rafinerska raised its prices by 330 crowns per tonne for natural (regular unleaded) and 300 crowns per tonne for all other types of gasoline.
- Unipetrol, the petrochemical holding company announced, plans to buy 150 million crowns worth of flood bonds as a goodwill gesture towards flood victims.

- The Environment Ministry has ordered the mining company, TVX Bohemia from further gold prospecting in the Kasperske hills in southwest Bohemia. The mining company won rights to carry out prospecting in the region until March, 1999. Company officials did not rule out challenging the issue in court.
- Corporate insolvency rose during the first quarter of 1997, reaching a combined total of 130.1 billion crowns. This represents a year-on-year increase of 20 percent.

- Foresbank Zlin announced plans to sell its shares in ZDB Bohumin and Spolchemie Usti nad Labem. This indicates that the bank does not intend to purchase a stake in EPAS, a holding company recently established by ZDB and Spolchemie.
- The crown continued to strengthen yesterday on the interbank market, closing at 18.45 crowns to the mark.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Prague stock exchange is preparing to trade flood bonds on the stock market. Private investors or businesses who purchased flood bonds and decide to exchange them for currency before the 5-year maturity date will be able to sell them on the stock exchange.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Welfare payments and state employee salaries will be paid on schedule despite serious flooding which has placed a burden on the state budget. The Finance Ministry thus quelled fears of a repetition of payment delays experienced in June.

PRAVO - The Agricultural chamber is requesting export licences for 400,000 tonnes of wheat and 250,000 tonnes of rape seed oil. The inter-ministerial licensing commission, however, rejected an export licence application for this year's crop.
